definitions.gloss: apparently; it seems; it looks like
definitions.explanation: Indicates inference or conjecture based on evidence. The speaker is fairly confident but not completely certain.
Indicates that something was accomplished with difficulty or just barely managed.

examples.japanese: どうやら{彼|かれ}は{来|こ}ないらしい。
どうやら{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}りそうだ。
examples.english: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.japanese: どうやら{風邪|かぜ}を{引|ひ}いたらしく、{喉|のど}が{痛|いた}い。
examples.english: It seems I've caught a cold—my throat hurts.

examples.japanese: どうやら{間|ま}に{合|あ}った。
examples.english: Somehow, I made it in time.

examples.japanese: {難|むずか}しい{試験|しけん}だったが、どうやら{合格|ごうかく}できたようだ。
examples.english: It was a difficult exam, but it seems I somehow managed to pass.

examples.japanese: どうやら{無事|ぶじ}に{届|とど}いたみたいで{安心|あんしん}した。
examples.english: It seems it arrived safely, so I was relieved.

notes:
TWO MAIN USES:

1) INFERENCE: Apparently/It seems
・どうやら〜らしい/ようだ/みたいだ (it seems that ~)
・Based on observation, the speaker infers something

2) BARELY: Just managed
・どうやら〜た (somehow managed to ~)
・Implies difficulty but ultimate success

COMMON PATTERNS:
・どうやら〜らしい (apparently ~ / it seems ~)
・どうやら〜ようだ (it appears that ~)
・どうやら〜そうだ (it seems ~)

NUANCE:
どうやら suggests the speaker has some evidence but isn't completely certain. It's softer than はっきり (clearly) but more confident than もしかしたら (perhaps).

EXAMPLES OF SENSE 2:
・どうやら{無事|ぶじ}に{着|つ}いたようだ (It seems we've arrived safely somehow)
・どうやら{切|き}り{抜|ぬ}けた (Somehow got through it)
